flags.proposed: Describe the parametric approach as in Gregory: it links the counterparty's default intensity (credit spread) to portfolio exposure through a simple parametric function calibrated to the historical relationship between exposure and credit spreads (e.g. Hull-White: hazard rate = f(exposure; b)). Replace 'such as a multiplier on CVA'/'alpha multiplier on CVA' with 'such as a function linking the hazard rate to portfolio value calibrated to historical data'. The regulatory alpha multiplier is a capital device, not a WWR modelling method.
flags.source_says: Same wording in source (p42 option (a), p43 table).
flags.derivation: Gregory (and project notes CR-20 p): Parametric = 'Examines the historical link between portfolio exposure and credit spreads. High portfolio value together with a high credit spread indicates higher WWR'. Structural = maps default and exposure from a bivariate distribution. Hazard rate = simulate spreads and compute exposure at default at wider spreads, may underestimate WWR. Key (a) is still the best option because (b)-(d) are clearly false, but the parametric description misleads.
